svg.title: SDLC plugin layers
svg.desc: Layer map of the sdlc plugin by structure. Top to bottom: 17 commands, 21 skills grouped by orchestrator phase (Define, Build, Prove, Ship with Learn), 10 agents, scripts (verify.py proves a feature), templates, and the files written into the user's repo (.sdlc/, docs/sdlc/, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, knowledge/). Hooks (security-guidance, hookify, verify-freshness, prove-budget, model-router with role-guard and trust-anchor) run on six Claude Code events outside the stack, each started through sg-python.sh. Packaging, the other hosts' manifests, tests, docs and licenses sit underneath. At the bottom, the optional sdlc-extras companion plugin (plugins/sdlc-extras/, installed separately from the same marketplace) holds the Ralph loop with its Stop hook and setup script, hookify's list, configure and help commands, and the conversation-analyzer, type-design-analyzer, comment-analyzer and code-simplifier agents.
svg.text: How sdlc 1.8.1 is built, from what the user types down to what lands in their repo. Each band is one plugin structure and arrows show who calls whom.
Hooks sit outside the stack because Claude Code fires them, not the workflow.
start hands the feature to the orchestrator; other commands load one skill or run a script
dispatch fresh subagents with a phase-specific brief
commands and skills (not agents) run these for state and facts the model should not guess
